html:
The Yeidji, also spelt Yiiji and widely known as Gwini or Kwini, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northeast Kimberley in Western Australia. The map shows them as Yiiji from 1600 to 1815, west of Cambridge Gulf. They also count themselves among the Balanggarra, the people of the far northeast Kimberley.

Their neighbours included the Gajirrawoong and Miriwoong to the east and the Ngarinyin to the southwest. An Anglican mission was founded on the Forrest River in 1913. In 1926 a police party killed Aboriginal people in this part of the Kimberley, in the Forrest River massacre, which a Royal Commission looked into the next year.
